mainTopic: Lineage worries about exiled and mixed populations, followed by the opening of the second פרק on a brother born after his brother's death.
overview: The גמרא finishes naming the lands where the ten tribes were exiled, and רבי יוחנן says people from all of them are suspect in lineage. רב יהודה reports that שמואל told him not to worry, because a child of a non-Jewish mother is her child. The גמרא asks about the exiled Jewish women and answers that they became barren. A second version says the חכמים declared those groups full non-Jews, based on a פסוק in הושע. Next comes רב יהודה's teaching that the Jews will celebrate when תרמוד is destroyed, and a discussion of whether it already was. עולא praises רב המנונא but worries about his hometown, הרפניא, until he learns that רב המנונא belongs to פום נהרא. The גמרא then explains the name הרפניא and traces its flawed lineage through מישון and תרמוד back to עבדי שלמה. The first פרק ends, and the second פרק opens with a משנה about the wife of a brother who died before the new brother was born. רב נחמן begins the גמרא by saying both readings of that משנה are correct.

steps.title: Identifying the places where the ten tribes were exiled
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes matching each place name in the exile פסוק to a known location: חבור is חדייב, נהר גוזן is גינזק, and ערי מדי is חמדן (or ניהר) and the towns around it.
steps.simpleTranslation: [חבור] is חדייב. 'The river גוזן' is גינזק. 'The cities of מדי' are חמדן and its neighboring towns. Some say: ניהר and its neighboring towns.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues from the previous daf, explaining which real places match the names in the פסוק about the exile of the ten tribes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This matters because רב יהודה worries that non-Jews living in these places may descend from the ten tribes. So the גמרא needs to pin down exactly which regions are suspect. For 'the cities of מדי' there are two opinions: חמדן and its towns, or ניהר and its towns.

keyTerms.meaning: The ten tribes exiled by Assyria
Its 'friends', meaning the neighboring towns around it

phrases.english: This is Hadyab,
phrases.notes: This continues a list from the previous daf, explaining the word 'חבור' from the פסוק (מלכים ב 17:6).

phrases.english: 'The river of Gozan' — this is Ginzak,
'And the cities of Media' — this is Hamadan and its neighboring towns,
And some say: this is Nihar and its neighboring towns.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the place-by-place reading of the exile פסוק begun on the previous daf.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The exile locations are identified as חדייב, גינזק, and חמדן (or ניהר) with its neighboring towns.

steps.title: Which towns are the 'neighboring towns'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which towns are meant by 'its neighboring towns.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Its neighboring towns — which are they?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a simple clarifying question. It is setting up the next step, which will list the towns.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The previous step said 'חמדן and its neighboring towns' but never named them. Since these places will be under suspicion, the גמרא needs the exact list.

phrases.english: Its neighboring towns — which are they?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for details about a vague term used in Step 1.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The names of the towns around חמדן.

steps.title: שמואל names the neighboring towns
steps.stepSummary: שמואל lists the neighboring towns: כרך, מושכי, חידקי, and דומקי.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: כרך, מושכי, חידקי, and דומקי.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל answers the question by naming four towns.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the suspect area is clearly defined. It is not only the main city but also these four surrounding towns.

phrases.english: Shmuel said:
Kerakh, Mushkhei, Hidkei, and Domakya.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the question of Step 2.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The neighboring towns are כרך, מושכי, חידקי, and דומקי.

steps.title: All these places are suspect
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן rules that all these places are treated as disqualified because of the lineage concern.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: And all of them are for disqualification.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives the practical ruling: every place on this list falls under the concern.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Naming the places was not just geography. The point is that people from all these places carry a lineage worry, because they might descend from the ten tribes. So they are treated as disqualified.

keyTerms.meaning: For disqualification (treated as having a lineage problem)

steps.whyThisMatters: This turns the list of places into a practical halachic concern about lineage, which שמואל will push back on next.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yohanan said:
And all of them are for disqualification.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies a legal ruling to the places identified in Steps 1 to 3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: All the listed places are treated as disqualified because of the lineage concern.

steps.title: שמואל: a child of a non-Jewish mother is her child
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה reports that when he told שמואל about this concern, שמואל said not to worry. A Jewish man's son from a non-Jewish woman is not considered his son; he is hers.
steps.simpleTranslation: When I said this before שמואל, he said to me: Your son from a Jewish woman is called your son. But your son from a non-Jewish woman is not called your son, only her son.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה tells us how שמואל answered the worry: the children of exiled Jewish men and non-Jewish women are simply not Jewish.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry was that today's non-Jews in these lands might descend from the ten tribes. שמואל points out that a child follows the status of a non-Jewish mother. So descent through Jewish fathers and non-Jewish mothers produces non-Jews, and the worry goes away.

keyTerms.meaning: When I said it before him
Is called your son (counts as your child for lineage)

steps.confusionAlert: The 'I' here is רב יהודה, the one who raised the worry. He is reporting what שמואל told him. It is not שמואל speaking about himself.

phrases.aramaic: כִּי אַמְרִיתַהּ קַמֵּיהּ דִּשְׁמוּאֵל, אֲמַר לִי:
phrases.english: When I said it before Shmuel, he said to me:
phrases.notes: The speaker is רב יהודה, who raised the worry about the ten tribes on the previous daf.

phrases.aramaic: בִּנְךָ הַבָּא מִן יִשְׂרְאֵלִית קָרוּי בִּנְךָ,
phrases.english: Your son who comes from a Jewish woman is called your son,

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין בִּנְךָ הַבָּא מִן הַגּוֹיָה קָרוּי בִּנְךָ,
phrases.english: but your son who comes from a non-Jewish woman is not called your son,
rather, her son.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי אַמְרִיתַהּ קַמֵּיהּ דִּשְׁמוּאֵל, אֲמַר לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Pushes back on the lineage concern behind Step 4 by applying the rule that a child follows a non-Jewish mother.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A child born to a non-Jewish mother is her child and is not Jewish, so the descendants of exiled men who married non-Jewish women are not Jews.

steps.title: But what about the Jewish daughters?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges שמואל: there were also Jewish women in exile, and רבינא taught that a Jewish woman's son from a non-Jewish man is Jewish.
steps.simpleTranslation: But there are daughters! And רבינא said: Learn from this that your daughter's son from a non-Jewish man is called your son.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks שמואל's answer. His rule only covers Jewish men; it says nothing about Jewish women who had children there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Exiled Jewish women who had children with non-Jewish men would pass on Jewish status, as רבינא taught. So the descendants in those lands could still include Jews, and the worry returns.

keyTerms.meaning: But there is (a standard opener for a challenge)

phrases.english: But there are the daughters,
phrases.notes: He means the Jewish women of the ten tribes, who also went into exile.

phrases.english: and Ravina said: Learn from this,

phrases.aramaic: בֶּן בִּתְּךָ הַבָּא מִן הַגּוֹי קָרוּי בִּנְךָ!
phrases.english: your daughter's son who comes from a non-Jewish man is called your son!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges שמואל's answer in Step 5 by pointing to the gap it leaves.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's claim that the descendants in those lands are not Jewish.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Jewish women in exile would have Jewish children even from non-Jewish fathers, as רבינא taught, so some descendants would still be Jews.

steps.title: Those women became barren
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers with a tradition: the Jewish women of that generation became barren, so no Jewish descendants came through them.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a tradition that the daughters of that generation became barren.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge with a received tradition: those Jewish women never had children.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge only works if the exiled Jewish women had children. The tradition says they became barren. So all descendants came from Jewish men and non-Jewish women, and by שמואל's rule they are not Jewish.

keyTerms.meaning: We have a tradition (learned from teachers)

steps.whatToRemember: In this first version, שמואל removes the worry in two parts. Children of non-Jewish mothers are not Jewish, and the Jewish women of that generation had no children at all.

phrases.english: It is learned as a tradition that the daughters of that generation
became completely barren.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Factual tradition that removes the case behind the challenge.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Exiled Jewish women had Jewish children, so the descendants could include Jews.
steps.terutzMaskana: Those women became barren, so all descendants came through non-Jewish mothers and are not Jewish.

steps.title: Second version: the חכמים declared them full non-Jews
steps.stepSummary: Another version of שמואל's answer: the חכמים did not leave the place where they discussed this until they declared those people complete non-Jews.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: When I said this before שמואל, he said to me: They did not move from there until they made them complete non-Jews.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a different version of what שמואל told רב יהודה. This time the answer is a formal ruling, not a rule about mothers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version, the worry is removed because the חכמים declared these groups full non-Jews. It does not depend on whose children they were. So their marriages carry no Jewish status and raise no lineage concern.

keyTerms.meaning: They did not move from there

phrases.english: There are those who say:

phrases.aramaic: כִּי אַמְרִיתַהּ קַמֵּיהּ דִּשְׁמוּאֵל, אָמַר לִי:
phrases.english: When I said it before Shmuel, he said to me:
They did not move from there,
until they made them complete non-Jews,

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי: כִּי אַמְרִיתַהּ קַמֵּיהּ דִּשְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second version of שמואל's reply, replacing the approach of Steps 5 to 7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The חכמים formally declared those groups complete non-Jews, so there is no lineage concern.

steps.title: The פסוק: they bore strange children
steps.stepSummary: The second version is supported by הושע 5:7: 'They betrayed ה׳, for they bore strange children.'
steps.simpleTranslation: As it says: 'They have dealt treacherously against ה׳, for they have begotten strange children.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a פסוק to back up the claim that these people became complete non-Jews.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק calls their children 'strange', meaning foreign. This supports the idea that their descendants are treated as non-Jews and not as part of the Jewish people.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is said (introducing a פסוק)

steps.whatToRemember: There are two versions of שמואל's answer. In the first, the child follows a non-Jewish mother, and the Jewish women became barren. In the second, the חכמים declared them complete non-Jews, based on the פסוק in הושע. Either way, there is no lineage worry.

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״בַּה׳ בָּגָדוּ כִּי בָנִים זָרִים יָלָדוּ״.
phrases.english: As it is said: 'They have dealt treacherously against the Lord, for they have begotten strange children.'

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״בַּה׳ בָּגָדוּ כִּי בָנִים זָרִים יָלָדוּ״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the scriptural support for Step 8.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that those groups were made complete non-Jews.

steps.title: A future celebration when תרמוד is destroyed
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה teaches that the Jews will one day make a יום טוב when תרמוד is destroyed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף sat behind רב כהנא, and רב כהנא sat in front of רב יהודה. רב יהודה said: someday the Jews will make a festival when תרמוד is destroyed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets the scene, with students sitting before רב יהודה, and then gives his teaching: the destruction of תרמוד will be a reason to celebrate.
steps.deeperAnalysis: תרמוד is a city whose people have flawed lineage, as step 22 will show. The גמרא does not say why its destruction would be celebrated; given the lineage context, one likely reason is that it would stop that flawed lineage from mixing into the Jewish people.

keyTerms.meaning: A city whose people had flawed lineage
A festival day, a day of celebration

phrases.aramaic: יָתֵיב רַב יוֹסֵף אֲחוֹרֵיהּ דְּרַב כָּהֲנָא,
phrases.english: Rav Yosef sat behind Rav Kahana,

phrases.aramaic: וְיָתֵיב רַב כָּהֲנָא קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב יְהוּדָה
phrases.english: and Rav Kahana sat before Rav Yehuda,
and he sat and said:
phrases.notes: The speaker here is רב יהודה, the teacher they were sitting in front of.

phrases.english: In the future, the Jews will make a festival day
when Tarmod is destroyed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new teaching about a particular city whose lineage, as step 22 explains, is flawed; it follows the lineage theme but does not build on the argument of steps 5 to 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The destruction of תרמוד will be a cause for a יום טוב.

steps.title: But תרמוד was already destroyed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that תרמוד has already been destroyed.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it was already destroyed!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב יהודה: how can he speak of a future destruction if the city already fell?
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the destruction already happened, there is no future day left to celebrate. The teaching seems to describe something that is already over.

keyTerms.meaning: But look, here is a problem

phrases.english: But it was already destroyed!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יהודה's statement that תרמוד will be destroyed in the future
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A future event cannot be something that already happened.

steps.title: That was a different city, תמוד
steps.stepSummary: The city that was destroyed was תמוד, not תרמוד.
steps.simpleTranslation: That city was תמוד.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the destroyed city was a different one with a similar name, תמוד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two cities are treated as separate places. תרמוד itself still stands, so רב יהודה's teaching about the future still makes sense.

keyTerms.meaning: A different city with a similar name

phrases.english: That one was Tamud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 11.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The destroyed city was תרמוד itself.
steps.terutzMaskana: The destroyed city was תמוד, and תרמוד still stands.

steps.title: רב אשי: one city that keeps rebuilding itself
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי says תרמוד and תמוד are the same city, but it has two sides. When one side is destroyed, the other side is lived in.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: תרמוד and תמוד are the same city. It is a double city. When one side is destroyed, the other side is settled, and when that side is destroyed, this side is settled.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי gives a different answer to the challenge. It is one city, but it has never been destroyed completely.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier answer said these were two different cities. רב אשי says it is a single city with two halves that take turns being ruined and resettled. So the full destruction worth celebrating is still in the future.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
Tarmod is the same as Tamud,
but it is a doubled city:
phrases.notes: The letter in square brackets is part of the corrected wording.

phrases.aramaic: חֲרִיב מֵהַאי גִּיסָא — אִיתִּיב מֵהַאי גִּיסָא,
phrases.english: when it is destroyed on this side, it is settled on that side,

phrases.aramaic: (וְאִי) חֲרִיב מֵהַאי גִּיסָא — אִיתִּיב מֵהַאי גִּיסָא.
phrases.english: and when it is destroyed on that side, it is settled on this side.
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the word in round brackets. The meaning stays the same.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר: הַיְינוּ תַּרְמוֹד הַיְינוּ תָּמוֹד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives another answer to step 11 and rejects the idea from step 12 that these are two separate cities.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The partial destruction already counted as the destruction.
steps.terutzMaskana: The city has only been ruined one half at a time and has never been destroyed completely.

steps.title: עולא praises רב המנונא but hints at his hometown
steps.stepSummary: עולא admires רב המנונא's learning but says, 'if only he were not from הרפניא,' and רב המנונא is embarrassed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב המנונא sat in front of עולא, busy learning הלכה. עולא said: What a man, what a man! If only his town were not הרפניא! רב המנונא was embarrassed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story about lineage. עולא suggests that רב המנונא's hometown casts doubt on his family background.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The people of הרפניא were known for flawed lineage, so coming from there suggests a possible family problem. This sets up the next steps, where עולא checks where רב המנונא really belongs.

keyTerms.meaning: A town known for people of flawed lineage

phrases.english: Rav Hamnuna sat before Ulla
and was busy learning halakha.
He said: What a man, and what a man!
phrases.notes: The speaker is עולא, praising רב המנונא.

phrases.english: If only Harpanya were not his town!
He was embarrassed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new story on the same theme of places with flawed lineage.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Coming from הרפניא raises suspicion about a person's lineage.

steps.title: עולא asks where he pays his head tax
steps.stepSummary: עולא asks רב המנונא which town he pays his head tax to.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said to him: Where do you pay your head tax?
steps.whatsHappening: עולא asks a practical question to find out which town רב המנונא officially belongs to.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The town that collects a person's tax shows which town he is counted as part of. That can settle whether he is really a resident of הרפניא.

keyTerms.meaning: Head tax, a tax paid per person

phrases.english: He said to him: The head tax,
to where do you give it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows up on רב המנונא's embarrassment from step 14.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which town רב המנונא is officially counted with

steps.title: He pays it to פום נהרא
steps.stepSummary: רב המנונא answers that he pays his tax to פום נהרא.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: To פום נהרא.
steps.whatsHappening: רב המנונא answers that his tax goes to the town of פום נהרא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This shows that רב המנונא's place is officially counted under פום נהרא, not הרפניא.

keyTerms.meaning: A town whose people did not have flawed lineage

phrases.english: He said to him: To Pum Nahara.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from step 15.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He pays his tax to פום נהרא.

steps.title: So you belong to פום נהרא
steps.stepSummary: עולא concludes that רב המנונא belongs to פום נהרא, so his lineage is not suspect.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: If so, you are from פום נהרא.
steps.whatsHappening: עולא concludes that רב המנונא counts as a man of פום נהרא, which clears his name.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Where a person pays his tax decides which town he belongs to. Since רב המנונא belongs to פום נהרא, the suspicion attached to הרפניא does not apply to him.
steps.whatToRemember: עולא's worry about הרפניא was removed because רב המנונא pays his tax to פום נהרא, so he counts as a member of that town.

phrases.english: He said to him: If so,
you are from Pum Nahara.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from the answer in step 16.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רב המנונא belongs to פום נהרא, so his lineage is not suspect.

steps.title: What does the name הרפניא mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the name הרפניא means.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is הרפניא?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks about the meaning of the name הרפניא. This sets up the explanations that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer will connect the town's name to why its people have flawed lineage.

phrases.english: What is Harpanya?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to explain the name of the town mentioned in step 14.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of the name הרפניא

steps.title: רבי זירא: the mountain everyone turns to
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא explains that הרפניא means 'the mountain everyone turns to'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said: It is a mountain that everyone turns to.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא explains the name by splitting it into הר, 'mountain', and פונין, 'turn to'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The name suggests a place where everyone ends up, including people who could not marry elsewhere. That is why the lineage there is mixed.

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said:
A mountain that everyone turns to.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 18.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: הרפניא means 'a mountain that everyone turns to'.

steps.title: A ברייתא: those who do not know their family go there
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that anyone who does not know his family and tribe goes to הרפניא.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא teaches: anyone who does not know his family and his tribe goes there.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that fits רבי זירא's explanation and says exactly who 'turns to' הרפניא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי זירא said that everyone turns there. The ברייתא adds the detail: it is people who do not know their family line. This explains why the town has a reputation for flawed lineage.

keyTerms.meaning: It is taught in a ברייתא

phrases.english: It is taught in a baraita:
Anyone who does not know his family and his tribe
turns to there.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports and fills in רבי זירא's explanation in step 19.
steps.raayaObject: The explanation that הרפניא is where 'everyone turns'
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא saying that people who do not know their family and tribe go there

steps.title: רבא: הרפניא is deeper than שאול
steps.stepSummary: רבא says the flaw of הרפניא is deeper than שאול, because people can be saved from שאול but this flaw cannot be fixed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: It is deeper than שאול, as the פסוק says: 'From the power of שאול I will ransom them, from death I will redeem them.' But their flaw has no fix.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא uses a פסוק to show how serious the lineage problem of הרפניא is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק shows that a person can be rescued even from שאול. A flawed lineage, though, cannot be repaired, so it is 'deeper' than שאול.

keyTerms.meaning: The underworld, the place of the dead

phrases.english: Rava said:
And it is deeper than the netherworld,
as it is said:
'From the power of the netherworld I will ransom them,
from death I will redeem them,'
whereas their disqualification
has no remedy.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds how serious the flaw of the town described in steps 19 and 20 is.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The lineage flaw of הרפניא can never be fixed.

steps.title: The chain of flawed lineage back to עבדי שלמה
steps.stepSummary: The flaw of הרפניא comes from מישון, the flaw of מישון comes from תרמוד, and the flaw of תרמוד comes from עבדי שלמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The disqualified people of הרפניא are disqualified because of those of מישון. Those of מישון are disqualified because of those of תרמוד, and those of תרמוד are disqualified because of עבדי שלמה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא traces where the bad lineage came from, linking the towns in a chain back to its source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each town became flawed by marrying into the town before it. The source is עבדי שלמה, servants who mixed into the population. This also explains why the destruction of תרמוד in step 10 is a reason to celebrate.

keyTerms.meaning: A town near הרפניא with flawed lineage

steps.whatToRemember: The bad lineage goes in a chain: הרפניא from מישון, מישון from תרמוד, תרמוד from עבדי שלמה. That is why רב יהודה said the destruction of תרמוד will be celebrated.
steps.whyThisMatters: It connects the whole section, linking the story of הרפניא back to the teaching about תרמוד at the start.

phrases.english: The disqualified of Harpanya are because of the disqualified of Meishon,
and the disqualified of Meishon are because of the disqualified of Tarmod,
and the disqualified of Tarmod are because of Solomon's servants.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains where the flaw described in step 21 came from and ties it back to תרמוד in step 10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The flawed lineage of these towns traces back through תרמוד to עבדי שלמה.

steps.title: A popular saying matches the chain of flawed places
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a common saying about crooked measures sinking from שאול down to הרפניא, which matches the chain of flaws in steps 21-22.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this is what people say: A big measure and a small measure keep rolling down to the grave, from the grave to תרמוד, from תרמוד to מישן, and from מישן to הרפניא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up what it just said by showing that even everyday people have a saying with the same idea.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 21 said the flaw of הרפניא is deeper than שאול, and step 22 traced the flaws through תרמוד and מישן. The saying lists the same places in a downward order, ending at הרפניא as the lowest point. So the folk saying agrees that הרפניא is the very bottom, worse even than שאול.

keyTerms.meaning: And this is what people say: introduces a popular saying that fits the point
A קב, a unit of measure

steps.whatToRemember: The whole section ends with one picture: הרפניא is the lowest level, below even שאול, and both the חכמים and ordinary people say so.

phrases.english: And this is what people say:
A big measure and a small measure
phrases.notes: Two measures that don't match, the tools of a cheating seller who buys with the big one and sells with the small one.

phrases.english: keep rolling along down to the grave,
and from the grave to Tarmod, and from Tarmod to Meishan,
and from Meishan to Harpanya.
phrases.notes: Same places as steps 21-22, now in going-down order, with הרפניא at the very bottom.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the chain of flaws in step 22 with a popular saying
steps.raayaObject: That הרפניא is the lowest level, below שאול, and that the flaws pass down through תרמוד and מישן

steps.title: Hadran — Closing פרק חמש עשרה נשים
steps.stepSummary: The closing line for the first פרק of יבמות.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, חמש עשרה נשים.
steps.whatsHappening: This line marks the end of the first פרק, חמש עשרה נשים. A new פרק starts right after it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A הדרן is not part of the argument. It is a farewell to the פרק and a promise to come back and learn it again.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you: the closing words said at the end of a פרק
Fifteen women: the name of the first פרק of יבמות

phrases.english: We will return to you, Fifteen Women

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the פרק after the final aggadic discussion
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The first פרק of יבמות is complete.

steps.title: New פרק: the widow of a brother who died before you were born
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה describes אשת אחיו שלא היה בעולמו. A brother born after another brother already died does not do יבום with that brother's widow, and her צרה is also exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case of 'the wife of his brother who was not alive in his lifetime'? There were two brothers, and one died. Then a new brother was born. After that, the second brother did יבום with the dead brother's wife, and then he also died. The first widow is free to leave, because she is the wife of a brother who never lived at the same time as the new brother. The second widow is also free, because she is her צרה.
steps.whatsHappening: The new פרק opens by explaining one of the women from the list in the first פרק: the wife of a brother the new brother never overlapped with in life.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only a brother who was alive together with the dead brother can do יבום. The new baby was born after the first brother died, so the first brother's widow is forbidden to him. When the second brother dies, both of his wives come before the baby. The second brother's original wife is exempt too, because she is the צרה of a forbidden woman, like the rule from the first פרק.

keyTerms.meaning: The wife of his brother who was not alive in his lifetime: a brother who died before he was born
Did יבום, married the dead brother's childless widow
Goes out: she is free, with no יבום or חליצה
Her צרה: the other wife of the same husband

steps.confusionAlert: 'The first' and 'the second' here mean the two widows, not the two brothers. The first widow was the wife of the brother who died first, and the second widow was the second brother's own wife.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the whole new פרק. The rule that a צרה of a forbidden woman is also exempt now applies to this new kind of forbidden woman.

phrases.english: What is the case of the wife of his brother
who was not in his world?
phrases.notes: Literally 'not in his world', meaning that brother died before this one was born, so they were never alive together.

phrases.english: Two brothers, and one of them died,
and a brother was born to them,
and afterward the second brother did yibum
with his brother's wife, and then died.
The first widow goes out free

phrases.aramaic: מִשּׁוּם אֵשֶׁת אָחִיו שֶׁלֹּא הָיָה בְּעוֹלָמוֹ,
phrases.english: because she is the wife of his brother who was not alive in his lifetime,
and the second widow goes free because she is her co-wife.

steps.triggerLanguage: כֵּיצַד אֵשֶׁת אָחִיו שֶׁלֹּא הָיָה בְּעוֹלָמוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new פרק after the הדרן
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A brother born after another brother died does not do יבום with that brother's widow. If she becomes a צרה of another wife, that other wife is also exempt.

steps.title: If the second brother only made a מאמר
steps.stepSummary: If the second brother only did מאמר (a יבום-style betrothal) with the first widow and then died, his own wife must do חליצה and cannot do יבום.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the second brother only did מאמר with her and then died, the second widow does חליצה but does not do יבום.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה changes one detail. Here the second brother never fully married the first widow; he only made a מאמר with her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A מאמר is a first step toward יבום, not a full marriage. So the second widow is not fully the צרה of the forbidden woman and is not completely exempt. She still may not do יבום, so she must do חליצה.

keyTerms.meaning: A betrothal-type step done with a יבמה before full יבום
She does חליצה, the ceremony that frees her from יבום

steps.whatToRemember: Full יבום means the second wife is a full צרה and goes free completely. Only a מאמר means a middle result: חליצה, but no יבום.

phrases.english: If he made a ma'amar with her and died,
phrases.notes: 'He' is the second brother, and 'her' is the first brother's widow.

phrases.english: the second widow does chalitza and does not do yibum.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Changes the case in step 25 from full יבום to only a מאמר, which leads to a different result for the second widow
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the second brother only made a מאמר, the second widow does חליצה and may not do יבום.

steps.title: Both readings of the משנה are correct
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן says that people who read 'the first' and people who read 'the second' in the משנה are both correct. The גמרא then starts to explain each reading.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: רב נחמן said: Whoever reads 'the first' is not mistaken, and whoever reads 'the second' is not mistaken. Whoever reads...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens on the new משנה. רב נחמן says two different wordings of the משנה are both correct. The last words, 'whoever reads...', set up the next move, where the גמרא will explain why each reading works.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 25 the משנה said 'the first' widow goes out free, because she was the wife of the brother who died before the baby was born. Some read 'the second' there instead. רב נחמן does not choose between them. He says both wordings point to the same woman, the first brother's widow, each counted from a different angle.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that explains the משנה; here it marks the start of the גמרא on the new פרק
Whoever reads (or teaches) the משנה this way
Is not mistaken; his version is not wrong

steps.confusionAlert: רב נחמן is not saying there are two different women with two different laws. Both wordings describe the same woman, the first brother's widow who goes out free. They only count 'first' and 'second' from different starting points.

phrases.english: Gemara:
Rav Nachman said:
Whoever reads 'the first' is not mistaken,
phrases.notes: He means the line in the משנה about the widow who goes out free, the wife of the brother who died first.

phrases.english: whoever reads 'the second' is not mistaken.
Whoever reads...

steps.triggerLanguage: מאן דתני ראשונה לא משתבש, מאן דתני שניה לא משתבש
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the גמרא on the משנה from steps 25-26 by looking at how the widow who goes out free in step 25 is worded.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Both wordings of the משנה are correct: the widow who goes out free can be called 'the first' or 'the second'.
